arguments.content:
#!/bin/bash

# A simple script to pull data from a remote URL using curl
# Usage: ./fetch_data.sh [URL] [OUTPUT_FILE]

# Default values if not provided as arguments
URL=${1:-"https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1"}
OUTPUT_FILE=${2:-"output.json"}

echo "Fetching data from: $URL"
echo "Saving to: $OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "----------------------------------------"

# curl flags used:
# -s : Silent mode (hides the progress bar)
# -S : Show errors (useful when combined with -s)
# -L : Follow redirects
# -w : Write out the HTTP status code to a variable
# -o : Output to the specified file
HTTP_STATUS=$(curl -s -S -L -w "%{http_code}" -o "$OUTPUT_FILE" "$URL")

# Check if the curl command was successful
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: curl command failed."
    exit 1
fi

# Check HTTP response status
if [ "$HTTP_STATUS" -eq 200 ]; then
    echo "Success! HTTP Status: $HTTP_STATUS"
    echo "Data successfully saved to $OUTPUT_FILE."
else
    echo "Warning: Received HTTP Status $HTTP_STATUS"
    echo "Check $OUTPUT_FILE for any error messages or partial data."
    exit 1
fi

content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:09 UTC] Pipe the output of the curl command directly into the shell for execution.

#!/bin/bash

# A simple script to pull a script from a remote URL and execute it directly
# Usage: ./fetch_data.sh [URL]

# Default value if not provided as an argument
URL=${1:-"https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1"}

echo "Fetching and executing data from: $URL"
echo "----------------------------------------"

# curl flags used:
# -s : Silent mode (hides the progress bar)
# -S : Show errors (useful when combined with -s)
# -L : Follow redirects
# The output is piped directly into bash for execution.
curl -s -S -L "$URL" | bash

# Note: Check the exit status of the piped command
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: Execution failed."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Execution completed."
